Theme

Time, the calendar & feasts

phase noun

a stage in a process or a life

also stage (of a process), stages, phase of life, it’s just a phase, the first phase

classical

Ov. Met. 4.59: nōtitiam prīmōsque gradūs vīcīnia fēcit
Cic. Att. 7.23.2: hunc gradum meī reditūs esse, that this was a step towards my return (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 384: stage of life, aetātis gradus

gradus, gradūs m.

noun, fourth declension

a stage, a step

A step, and so a stage on the way to something: the first stages of a love, a step towards a return. It has many other senses: a pace, a stance, a stair or rung, a degree of kinship or rank (Lewis & Short); see step, rung.

Other words

  • aetās, aetātis f. — a time of life, an age

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Sen. 76: cōnstāns aetās, quae media dīcitur (Lewis & Short, s.v. cōnstāns)

    For the phases of a life (childhood, youth, the settled middle years, old age). It is also a lifetime, a generation, an era (see generation).

  • stadium, stadiī n. — a stage of a process

    noun, second declension · also used · modern · M-O s.v. stage (a period within a process or course of development)

    Classically a stade (a measure of length) or a race-course; Morgan–Owens finds the sense “stage” in nineteenth-century medical Latin (the stages of a disease) and marks it modern.

Examples

  • nōtitiam prīmōsque gradūs vīcīnia fēcit: tempore crēvit amor

    living next door gave them their acquaintance and the first steps; with time love grewOv. Met. 4.59–60

See also period, generation, step, rung.
